chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhl from Ali ibn Uqbah from the wife of al-Hasan al-Sayqal from al-Hasan al-Sayqal from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
He was asked: How do women pray over the funeral if there is no man with them? He said: 'They line up all together, and no woman should precede them.'
ai.seo_question: How do women perform the funeral prayer when there are no men present?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the procedural details of women performing Salat al-Janazah independently, emphasizing that they form a single collective row (saff) without a distinct leader standing ahead, mirroring the general principle of female congregational prayer. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly view that women’s funeral prayer is valid and complete even without a male imam, provided the communal structure is maintained. The emphasis on uniformity underscores the importance of order (nizam) in ritual acts regardless of gender.
